messages:
maria: Quick thread — we need a final decision on rate-limiting semantics for API keys/orgs to handle fleet saturation. I sketched a capacity-proportional token-bucket approach. Thoughts?

 tom: short version pls? :)

 maria: idea: each API key + org has a token-bucket whose refill_rate is a function of the live GPU pool utilization for the region/pool that would serve the request. when utilization is high -> refill slows, effectively throttling at source.

 asha: so dynamic refill based on pool metrics. That sounds promising for graceful degradation. how do we avoid thundering bursts when utilization drops quickly?

 maria: two parts: 1) give a small burst allowance (credits accumulate up to burst cap). 2) use a short admission queue + priority score (paying customers or high-SLO routes get priority).

 rob: implementation note: we need counters close to the routing decision. Redis central is fine but must be sharded by pool to avoid cross-region latency. we should store bucket state as: ratelimit:pool:{pool}:org:{org}:key:{key} -> tokens, last_refill_ts

 kevin: what about leaky-bucket instead? simpler drain semantics and avoids token underflow issues.

 maria: leaky-bucket is simpler but less bursty friendly. token-bucket lets us honor short bursts for interactive latency. hybrid possible: token-bucket for ingress, leaky-bucket for long-running queue drain.

 infra-bot: Current pool util metrics: pool-eu-west-1 util=0.86, pool-us-east-1 util=0.41, avg-serving-latency=78ms

 asha: API semantics: return 429 with Retry-After when bucket empty. Also add headers with queue position and pool-id so clients can show progressive backoff. Eg: X-Redwood-Ratelimit: org=120/240; key=10/30

 tom: can we return a hint about expected wait time computed from queue length + avg token refill? that helps clients implement jitter/backoff.

 maria: yes, approximate ETA ok. We'll expose X-Redwood-Estimate-Seconds. We must guard against leaking internal metrics (low risk but check perms).

 rob: concerning correctness under races: we should use a compare-and-set update in Redis or Lua script that does refill+consume atomically. Example pseudo-lua:

 ```lua
 local key = KEYS[1]
 local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
 local rate = tonumber(ARGV[2]) -- tokens/sec
 local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[3])
 local cost = tonumber(ARGV[4])
 local s = redis.call('HMGET', key, 'tokens', 'ts')
 local tokens = tonumber(s[1]) or capacity
 local ts = tonumber(s[2]) or 0
 local delta = math.max(0, now - ts)
 tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + delta * rate)
 if tokens < cost then return {0, tokens} end
 tokens = tokens - cost
 redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', tokens, 'ts', now)
 return {1, tokens}
 ```

 kevin: nice. We'll need TTLs to GC keys for inactive orgs. Also shard keys by pool to keep locality.

 asha: fairness: we should have hierarchical checks: 1) per-key bucket, 2) per-org bucket, 3) per-pool catch-all. If a single key hogs, org bucket prevents blowing others. If org overall is abusive, org bucket gates it.

 maria: also support route weights: heavy model routes (long tokens) consume more tokens. e.g., generation r=1 token per token; embeddings r=0.2 per token unit. config example:

 ```yaml
 routes:
   - name: text-gen
     cost_multiplier: 1.0
   - name: embeddings
     cost_multiplier: 0.25
 ```

 rob: backpressure strategy when pool saturated: 1) slow refill (token logic), 2) short in-memory queue (N=500 per pool) with scoring for priority, 3) when queue full -> reject or route to cheaper region/model fallback.

 infra-bot: note: routing fallback to other region adds latency + egress cost. estimated extra $0.12 per request for eu->us fallback at current rates.

 tom: operational alerts? we need telemetry: token_exhausted count, avg_queue_wait, reject_rate, refill_rate_adjustments. tie to oncall SLOs.

 kevin: rollout plan: PoC in eu-west with token-bucket per-key + org bucket + Lua scripts in Redis cluster. Start with soft limits (log-only), then 10% traffic with queueing, then ramp.

 maria: can someone draft the config schema? I propose fields: pool_selector, refill_function(type=static|capacity_proportional, params), burst_cap, cost_multiplier_per_route, queue_size, priority_weights.

 asha: happy to own schema PR. I'll ping infra & security for review (data exposure for estimate headers).

 rob: final question: do we allow unlimited bursts for paid tiers? we can give a higher burst cap but it still must be gated by pool-level pool_utilization factor to avoid denial of service on hot pools.

 maria: agreed. paid_tier = higher burst & priority but still multiply refill by (1 - util)^alpha so when util→1, refill→0 for everyone.

 deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/ratelimit-poc -> staging at 2026-03-18T14:30Z :white_check_mark:

 maria: thanks all — action items: asha PR schema, rob Lua scripts + benchmarks, kevin telemetry dashboard. We'll sync next Wed to decide rollout %. :thumbsup:
